hero.headline: JetBlue canceling Vero Beach to JFK route in September due to low demand
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He explained that JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said. However, the Boston route is performing well. "Boston is seeing great demand," Dambeck said.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He emphasized the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time.

Dambeck said the door is not closed on the route returning in the future. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

cards.headline: Declassified records show Chinese actor downloaded Florida voter registration data in 2022
cards.teaser: Newly released White House intelligence records show a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter registration information from commercial websites in 2022.
cards.body:
Declassified records released by the Trump White House show a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter registration information from commercial websites in 2022. The same actor also obtained records from Colorado, Connecticut, Michigan, Oklahoma and Rhode Island. Another intelligence record lists Florida among 18 states whose voter information was obtained for possible identity matching and public-opinion analysis. The records describe the collection of voter information, some of it publicly available, but do not say Florida ballots or vote totals were altered. The 2022 report also says the actor's motive was unknown.

President Donald Trump did not single out Florida during his Thursday address, but records released by his White House did reference the state. Trump urged Congress to adopt tighter voting restrictions and repeated claims about the 2020 election that have not been substantiated. The White House characterized the broader collection effort as a major compromise of American voter data. However, an earlier federal assessment of the 2022 elections found no evidence that detected foreign cyber activity prevented voting, changed votes or compromised the integrity of ballots.

cards.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast seeks fosters and adopters during shelter renovation
cards.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation.
cards.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation. The construction will modernize the shelter, improve animal living spaces, enhance adoption areas, and create more comfortable and visible spaces to care for animals. However, the renovation presents significant challenges for the animals, who are being held in smaller spaces during the work.

Sarah Fisher of the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast said the animals are really being affected by the sound of the construction. It's very loud and the sound being in a closed kennel can be very stressful for an animal, Fisher said. About 50 animals are currently in foster care, but the shelter is hoping to get the remaining 67 animals housed on-site either fostered or adopted, with most of them being dogs. The shelter continues to receive animals daily and is on a mission to get them out as quickly as they come in.

cards.headline: Security ramped up for World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey
cards.teaser: Federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies are implementing a security plan two years in the making for Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain. The match has the highest possible security designation as a Level 1 Special Event.
cards.body:
A joint operations center in New York has overseen security and monitored threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team monitoring the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. For Sunday's match, FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel said the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there's anything that needs to be done from a threat perspective. The final will include a Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation.

The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security. When Trump attended an NBA Finals game last month in New York, police shut down several city blocks around the arena and fans were forced to wait in extra-long lines to go through enhanced security.

cards.headline: Democratic Rep. Nixon gets September trial date on Capitol sit-in charges
cards.teaser: Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May protest outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office.
cards.body:
Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon learned Wednesday she will face trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges related to her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Nixon and other protesters occupied the area for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map, which could help Republicans add up to four seats in the U.S. House. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave.

Nixon calls the prosecution political and has incorporated the case into her campaign for U.S. Senate. She is challenging retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman for the Democratic Senate nomination in Florida's Aug. 18 primary. Nixon said following Wednesday's hearing that if they think the threat of a trial is going to make her back down, they picked the wrong woman.

The trial is scheduled after Florida's Aug. 18 primary election. The case centers on Nixon's refusal to comply with police orders during the protest against the congressional redistricting map.

cards.headline: Florida gubernatorial candidate Fishback faces court fight over residency requirement
cards.teaser: Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback will defend his eligibility to remain in the primary next week as an opponent challenges whether he meets Florida's seven-year residency requirement.
cards.body:
Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback will defend his eligibility to remain in the primary during a two-day hearing scheduled to begin Tuesday in Tallahassee. Lt. Jay Collins, one of Fishback's opponents, argues that records showing Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., mean he does not satisfy Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governor. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida and maintained the state as his permanent home.

Because primary ballots have already been printed, the judge has said a ruling against Fishback could require election officials to post notices and decline to count votes cast for him. The case will determine whether Fishback remains on the Republican primary ballot for the gubernatorial race.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major I-95 Ramp Closures Planned July 19-24
cards.teaser:
Motorists across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 17-24 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department
cards.body:
Motorists across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 17-24 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report highlights multiple full road and ramp closures expected to have the greatest impact on drivers.

## Major closures to know about

### Southbound I-95 exit to Bridge Road closing overnight

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, also known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

Motorists will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt-Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road.

The closure is needed for roadway construction. FDOT has scheduled July 26-30 as contingency dates in case the work is delayed by weather or other unforeseen conditions.

### Martin Highway ramps closing at I-95

Two ramps serving Martin Highway at I-95 will close overnight from **Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to Martin Highway at Exit 110 will be closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Drivers will continue north to Becker Road at Exit 114, travel west on Becker Road and use southbound I-95 to return to the Martin Highway exit.

The northbound I-95 entrance ramp from Martin Highway will also be closed during the same hours. Motorists will be detoured east on Martin Highway, north on Newfield Parkway and west on Becker Road to reach the northbound I-95 entrance ramp.

FDOT said only one ramp closure will occur at a time.

### Orange Avenue exit closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

Drivers will be detoured to the eastbound Orange Avenue exit, north on Jenkins Road and west on Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The work includes paving and lighting installation. Contingency dates are scheduled for July 26-30.

### Emergency repairs could cause major delays on I-95

Southbound I-95 between Kanner Highway and Bridge Road will have **two lanes closed beginning at 4 p.m. Monday, July 20, and Tuesday, July 21.** The lanes are scheduled to reopen by 5:30 a.m. each morning.

FDOT said the closures are needed to complete an emergency repair near mile marker 98. Drivers are encouraged to consider alternate routes because the early closure time could affect the evening commute.

### Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads may close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several roads near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project. Closures may begin at **7 a.m. Monday, July 20, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 24,** on portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue.

The roads will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. Adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained throughout the work.

Detours will use nearby roads including SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and SW McDevitt Avenue. FDOT is also providing advance notice that SW Paar Drive between SW McIntosh Street and SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard may close from July 27-31.

## Martin County traffic impacts

Northbound and southbound I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line will continue to have two lanes closed overnight for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

U.S. 1 between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue may have two lanes closed intermittently from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times Monday through Friday for pavement widening and drainage work. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic through the work zone.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday for milling and resurfacing.

In Stuart, two westbound lanes on Monterey Road between Ocean Boulevard and Monterey Commons Boulevard may close from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. Tuesday through Thursday.

## St. Lucie County traffic impacts

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight from Sunday through Friday for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during daytime and overnight hours.

SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard will have intermittent lane closures from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road for milling and repaving.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road will continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures as part of the widening project.

## North Causeway marine restrictions continue

Boaters traveling near the North Causeway Bridge in Fort Pierce could encounter partial or full channel closures as crews continue removing sections of the former drawbridge.

Partial channel restrictions may occur during daylight hours on weekdays through late 2026. At least 45 feet of the channel is expected to remain open during partial closures.

Intermittent full channel closures lasting up to six hours may occur through July for the removal of steel bascule bridge spans. Vessels requiring full channel access must provide the bridge tender with 120 minutes of advance notice.

The new North Causeway Bridge remains open to vehicle traffic, although nearby roads including U.S. 1, Old Dixie Highway, Juanita Avenue and Harbortown Drive may have lane restrictions.

## Indian River County traffic impacts

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

I-95 near the new Oslo Road interchange may have one or two lanes closed overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for roadway construction.

Drivers near Sebastian Inlet should expect intermittent lane and shoulder closures on A1A from July 20-31. Flaggers will direct traffic through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park remain closed during construction of the replacement bridge, although the park, boat ramp and portions of both parking areas remain open.

## Additional I-95 closures coming the following week

FDOT is also providing advance notice of several closures scheduled to begin Sunday, July 26. All four I-95 ramps at Midway Road are expected to close separately overnight through July 31 for paving. Only one ramp will close at a time.

Detours will use St. Lucie West Boulevard, U.S. 1 and nearby interstate exits. Additional ramp closures are also planned later at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway.

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Drivers should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time interstate traffic conditions are available through [Florida 511](https://fl511.com). Updated lane closure information is available through [FDOT District Four](https://www.fdot.gov/info/co/district4).

cards.headline: Argentina rallies past England 2-1 to reach World Cup final
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and Argentina scored twice in the final minutes to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinals. The defending champions will face Spain in Sunday's final in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
cards.body:
Argentina rallied from a 1-0 deficit to defeat England 2-1 on Wednesday with goals from Enzo Fernandez and substitute Lautaro Martinez in the World Cup semifinals. England captain Harry Kane scored the opening goal in the 55th minute before Argentina's comeback in the final five minutes of the match.

Fernandez scored the equalizer in the 85th minute after receiving a pass from Lionel Messi and sweeping the ball in from outside the box. Martinez headed in the winner two minutes into stoppage time from a Messi cross. Martinez said he told teammate Alexis Mac Allister before the match that he would come on as a substitute and win the game.

The defending champions will face European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team proved itself after falling behind and showed the collectiveness and brotherhood that has defined their tournament run. England has now lost in the World Cup semifinals three times after previous defeats to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018.

cards.headline: Messi and Yamal to face off in World Cup final nearly two decades after iconic photo
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal will face each other in Sunday's World Cup final, nearly two decades after photographer Joan Monfort captured images of a teenage Messi bathing baby Yamal in a Barcelona charity photo shoot.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró near Barcelona who wanted to participate in the photo shoot. Messi was 20 years older than Yamal, who was a baby at the time. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble, and Yamal erupted at the club two years later. Now the 19-year-old Yamal will face Messi in Sunday's World Cup final when Argentina plays Spain.

Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press from his home in Barcelona, had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship when Yamal led Spain to the title. The photo went viral during that tournament, and interest has skyrocketed with the World Cup final approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos from professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without credit or compensation. Monfort, 58, a lifelong Barcelona supporter, said his heart is split between wanting Messi or Yamal to win.

cards.headline: MLB restricts dugout iPad use to prevent AI from making game decisions
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night to prevent artificial intelligence from helping make in-game decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started. In many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches, according to a June 11 memo from MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword. The memo was sent to general managers, assistant general managers and video coordinators.

A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead time to make any necessary adjustments, Sword wrote. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021. The tablets continue to have access to video and league-provided data.

cards.headline: Flip City gymnasts from Treasure Coast earn national top 15 finish, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.body:
Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine each found their way to gymnastics through different paths but now compete together as one unit. Rose-Daris said her entry into the sport started with a simple skill. "It wasn't really gymnastics, it was the fact that I knew how to do a cartwheel," she said. Supan was drawn to gymnastics after watching videos online. "All the gymnasts that I saw on YouTube, and how amazing they are, and how fun it looks," she said. Rine said she loves gymnastics because "I learn new things."

The trio competed locally, traveled, and advanced to states and regionals during what Head Coach Candice Lazuka called a strong season. At nationals in Knoxville, the gymnasts came close to achieving a perfect score. "It's hard to get a perfect 10, but we got a 9.9 and were very close to a 10," Lazuka said. Rose-Daris is looking forward to the upcoming competition in Iowa. "It's going to be really fun that I'm going to an entire different part of the world," she said. Supan described her feelings as "happy and exciting at the same time." Rine said she is focused on "getting first place on floors" at the Junior Olympics.

hero.headline: Downtown Delray Beach launches Wellness Pass with free fitness classes and spa discounts
hero.teaser: The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority created a mobile pass offering free classes and wellness deals for July and August.
hero.body:
The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August. The mobile-exclusive pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses throughout Downtown Delray Beach. The pass does not require an app download.

The program features free fitness classes, yoga sessions, spa discounts and wellness-focused offers across the downtown district. Miller Physical Therapy is participating with wellness-related services and promotions. The program arrives as wellness tourism and fitness-focused experiences continue to grow in popularity across South Florida, with consumers seeking affordable ways to stay active, reduce stress and support local businesses during the summer months.

cards.headline: Delray Beach dance studio plans Bridgerton-style masquerade gala July 24
cards.teaser: Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach is celebrating nine years with a themed anniversary gala and launching new Saturday dance classes.
cards.body:
Fred Astaire Dance Studios Delray Beach, located at 247 SE Sixth Ave., is hosting a Bridgerton-style masquerade gala on July 24. The studio is owned by world champion dancers Mar Martinez and Clifton Sepulveda. The anniversary gala will feature themed décor and dancing to celebrate the studio's nine years in business.

The studio is launching a Summer Boot Camp series beginning July 18 and continuing every Saturday through August. The classes are designed to help participants learn ballroom and Latin dance fundamentals. The studio is also hosting a DJ Latin Dance Night open to the public on July 31 from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m.

Martinez and Sepulveda are also preparing to teach a dance class at Florida Atlantic University beginning in August. The studio welcomes dancers of all experience levels, from beginners to competitive performers.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Zoo extends Kids Free promotion through August 10
cards.teaser: Palm Beach Zoo has extended its popular Kids Free promotion and announced the return of adults-only Wild Night Out events.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach Zoo has extended its Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10, according to Amanda Joiner, the zoo's chief marketing and technology officer, who shared updates during WPTV's "Shining A Light" segment from the zoo Monday morning. Under the program, up to four children ages 3 to 12 receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket. Joiner said the extension is designed to help local families enjoy affordable outings during the hottest stretch of summer while still supporting the zoo's conservation mission. Zoo officials emphasized that families still receive the full zoo experience through the promotion, including access to exhibits, shaded walkways and animal encounters. The zoo is also encouraging visitors to stay cool with indoor spaces, shaded pathways and frozen treats available throughout the park.

The zoo announced the return of its Wild Night Out series, an adults-only after-hours experience happening on the last Saturdays of July, August and September. The themed nights include Paws & Santa Claus in July, Tails & Touchdowns in August and Decades After Dark in September. The events will feature live entertainment, themed activities and performances from bands including Whiskey Six and Snapback. July's event will also serve as an early preview of this year's Zoo Lights celebration, with new lighting displays, updated activations and a noticeably different experience compared to previous years. The zoo's newest koala joey is officially a boy and has been named Bonza, which Joiner said is Australian slang for awesome or excellent.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth backs Blue Angels low-altitude Pensacola beach flyover
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is defending a Blue Angels jet that flew so low over a Pensacola beach Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying and sand kicked up.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote on his personal X account Thursday morning that the flyovers will continue until morale improves, one day after video spread widely on social media showing a Navy Blue Angels jet flying so low over a crowded Pensacola beach that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears. The U.S. Navy said in a statement shortly after Wednesday's incident that it was conducting a thorough safety review. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell wrote "Carry on Patriots" on social media alongside a photo showing a Blue Angels jet with a wingtip just feet above the heads of beachgoers. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings.

It is at least the third time that Hegseth and others have voiced support for military aviators performing maneuvers that have drawn public scrutiny and military investigations. In two prior cases, Hegseth's remarks led to the end of the safety investigations. Aviation safety consultant Jeff Guzzetti, who investigated crashes for the National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration, said a cavalier attitude like that can only lead to accidents. Flyovers at low altitudes like these have been linked to a number of past crashes, Guzzetti said.

cards.headline: Vindman raises $8.5 million in Florida U.S. Senate race, expands fundraising lead
cards.teaser: Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Alex Vindman raised $8.5 million during the second quarter, pushing his total receipts above $16 million in the race for Marco Rubio's former seat.
cards.body:
Retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman tightened his grip on the Democratic money lead during the second quarter, raising $8.5 million and pushing his total receipts above $16 million. Vindman said Republicans woke up with a bit of a panic and there is no denying that the Florida Senate race is in play. Vindman is challenging Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon for the Democratic Senate nomination in Florida's August 18 primary.

Republican Sen. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million. Her campaign also promoted polling showing her leading either Vindman or Nixon in a potential general-election matchup. Moody was appointed to the Senate after Marco Rubio resigned to become secretary of state. The November special election will determine who serves the final two years of Rubio's term.

cards.headline: Pensacola beachgoer calls Blue Angels low flyover a once-in-a-lifetime experience
cards.teaser: Florida beachgoer Alexandra Belcher said the Blue Angels flyover in Pensacola this week was a blessing to witness, despite the jet flying so low that sand kicked up and chairs went flying.
cards.body:
Florida beachgoer Alexandra Belcher, 34, called the Blue Angels flyover this week a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Belcher said she did not realize how close the jet was until everyone around her remarked on it. She said it was not normal, but it was such a blessing to be able to witness that with everybody that she was with. Video spreading widely on social media shows a jet from the Navy's demonstration squadron flying so low over a crowded beach in Pensacola on Wednesday that chairs and tents went flying, sand kicked up and children held their hands over their ears.

The U.S. Navy said in a statement shortly afterward that it was conducting a thorough safety review. On Thursday morning, acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said the Navy had no problem with the flight and there would be no reprimands or firings. Cao's post said Thursday that the Blue Angels conducted a flight debrief. Navy officials would not say if that debrief was the thorough safety review the Navy said it would conduct the day prior. A Navy official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to share internal planning, said the Blue Angels' next show on Saturday will go on as scheduled.

hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap as needs outpace available money
hero.teaser: Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall, and the gap between what the county needs and what it can afford could shape how residents get around for decades.
hero.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next 20 years, a gap that could determine how residents travel for decades to come.

The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements through 2050, but only $701 million is currently available. That means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Nearly all of the available funding comes from state and federal sources, with only $10 million coming from local revenue. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August and outlines transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. Without funding for these widening projects, the county will be unable to address growing congestion on these corridors.

State Road 710 stands out as among the county's highest priorities and has been the subject of repeated safety concerns. About $300 million in projects are planned for the corridor, reflecting the urgent need for improvements on this route. The massive funding shortfall highlights the challenge facing Martin County as it tries to balance transportation demands with limited financial resources over the coming decades.

cards.headline: FDOT to Hold Public Workshops on Willoughby Boulevard Improvement Study
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Transportation will hold two public workshops to discuss proposed improvements along Willoughby Boulevard between Monterey Road and U.S. 1 in Martin Count
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Transportation will hold two public workshops to discuss proposed improvements along Willoughby Boulevard between Monterey Road and U.S. 1 in Martin County.

The meetings are part of a Project Development and Environment, or PD&E, study examining potential alternatives for the corridor. FDOT will offer the workshop in virtual and in-person formats, and each meeting will include a presentation followed by an opportunity for residents to ask questions and provide feedback.

## Virtual workshop scheduled for July 28

The virtual workshop will begin at **5:30 p.m. Tuesday, July 28.** Participants must register in advance at [https://tinyurl.com/Willoughby-APW](https://tinyurl.com/Willoughby-APW).

People who prefer to join by phone can call **1-469-423-0557** and enter access code 35124623#.

Registered participants will receive an email containing a link to join the meeting. Those attending from a mobile device will need the free Microsoft Teams application. FDOT recommends allowing enough time to log in before the presentation begins.

## In-person workshop scheduled for July 29

The in-person workshop will begin at **5:30 p.m. Wednesday, July 29,** at the 10th Street Community Center, 724 SE 10th Street, Stuart, FL 34994.

The meeting will use an open-house format. FDOT staff will be available to explain the proposed alternatives, answer questions and assist attendees.

Questions and comments will be addressed in the order they are received. If a question cannot be answered during the event, FDOT will provide a written response after the meeting. Residents may also submit questions or comments before the workshop by contacting the project manager.

## What the study will evaluate

A PD&E study is an early phase of the transportation planning process used to evaluate possible improvements and determine how a project could move forward.

The process typically considers traffic operations, roadway safety, environmental effects, community impacts, engineering needs and estimated costs. Feedback gathered during the workshops will help FDOT evaluate the proposed alternatives for Willoughby Boulevard.

## Accessibility accommodations available

Anyone requiring accommodations under the Americans with Disabilities Act should contact FDOT at least seven days before the meeting.

Accommodation requests may be directed to FDOT Project Manager Vanita Saini, P.E., at **954-777-4468** or [Vanita.Saini@dot.state.fl.us](mailto:Vanita.Saini@dot.state.fl.us). Written requests may be mailed to the Florida Department of Transportation, 3400 West Commercial Boulevard, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33309.

People with hearing or speech impairments may contact the Florida Relay Service at 1-800-955-8771 for TDD service or 1-800-955-8770 for voice service.

For additional project information, contact Saini at 954-777-4468 or toll-free at 866-336-8435, extension 4468.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce woman wins $5 million on $20 scratch-off ticket
hero.body:
Maria Duran, 57, of St. Lucie County claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6, Florida Lottery officials announced Friday. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time lump-sum payment of $3,262,138.

Duran purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The $20 scratch-off game offers an overall odds of winning of 1-in-2.90.

The odds of winning the $5 million top prize in this game are 1-in-4,018,135, according to lottery officials. The announcement came several months after Duran claimed her prize in April.

The Florida Lottery released the information Friday as part of its regular announcements of major prize winners across the state. PK 2 Quick Mart will receive a bonus commission for selling the winning ticket.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major I-95 Ramp Closures Planned July 19-24
hero.teaser:
Motorists across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 17-24 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department
hero.body:
Motorists across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 17-24 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report highlights multiple full road and ramp closures expected to have the greatest impact on drivers.

## Major closures to know about

### Southbound I-95 exit to Bridge Road closing overnight

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, also known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

Motorists will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt-Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road.

The closure is needed for roadway construction. FDOT has scheduled July 26-30 as contingency dates in case the work is delayed by weather or other unforeseen conditions.

### Martin Highway ramps closing at I-95

Two ramps serving Martin Highway at I-95 will close overnight from **Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to Martin Highway at Exit 110 will be closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Drivers will continue north to Becker Road at Exit 114, travel west on Becker Road and use southbound I-95 to return to the Martin Highway exit.

The northbound I-95 entrance ramp from Martin Highway will also be closed during the same hours. Motorists will be detoured east on Martin Highway, north on Newfield Parkway and west on Becker Road to reach the northbound I-95 entrance ramp.

FDOT said only one ramp closure will occur at a time.

### Orange Avenue exit closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from **8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 19, through Thursday, July 23.**

Drivers will be detoured to the eastbound Orange Avenue exit, north on Jenkins Road and west on Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The work includes paving and lighting installation. Contingency dates are scheduled for July 26-30.

### Emergency repairs could cause major delays on I-95

Southbound I-95 between Kanner Highway and Bridge Road will have **two lanes closed beginning at 4 p.m. Monday, July 20, and Tuesday, July 21.** The lanes are scheduled to reopen by 5:30 a.m. each morning.

FDOT said the closures are needed to complete an emergency repair near mile marker 98. Drivers are encouraged to consider alternate routes because the early closure time could affect the evening commute.

### Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads may close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several roads near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project. Closures may begin at **7 a.m. Monday, July 20, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 24,** on portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue.

The roads will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. Adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained throughout the work.

Detours will use nearby roads including SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and SW McDevitt Avenue. FDOT is also providing advance notice that SW Paar Drive between SW McIntosh Street and SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard may close from July 27-31.

## Martin County traffic impacts

Northbound and southbound I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line will continue to have two lanes closed overnight for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

U.S. 1 between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue may have two lanes closed intermittently from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times Monday through Friday for pavement widening and drainage work. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic through the work zone.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday for milling and resurfacing.

In Stuart, two westbound lanes on Monterey Road between Ocean Boulevard and Monterey Commons Boulevard may close from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. Tuesday through Thursday.

## St. Lucie County traffic impacts

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight from Sunday through Friday for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during daytime and overnight hours.

SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard will have intermittent lane closures from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road for milling and repaving.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road will continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures as part of the widening project.

## North Causeway marine restrictions continue

Boaters traveling near the North Causeway Bridge in Fort Pierce could encounter partial or full channel closures as crews continue removing sections of the former drawbridge.

Partial channel restrictions may occur during daylight hours on weekdays through late 2026. At least 45 feet of the channel is expected to remain open during partial closures.

Intermittent full channel closures lasting up to six hours may occur through July for the removal of steel bascule bridge spans. Vessels requiring full channel access must provide the bridge tender with 120 minutes of advance notice.

The new North Causeway Bridge remains open to vehicle traffic, although nearby roads including U.S. 1, Old Dixie Highway, Juanita Avenue and Harbortown Drive may have lane restrictions.

## Indian River County traffic impacts

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

I-95 near the new Oslo Road interchange may have one or two lanes closed overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for roadway construction.

Drivers near Sebastian Inlet should expect intermittent lane and shoulder closures on A1A from July 20-31. Flaggers will direct traffic through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park remain closed during construction of the replacement bridge, although the park, boat ramp and portions of both parking areas remain open.

## Additional I-95 closures coming the following week

FDOT is also providing advance notice of several closures scheduled to begin Sunday, July 26. All four I-95 ramps at Midway Road are expected to close separately overnight through July 31 for paving. Only one ramp will close at a time.

Detours will use St. Lucie West Boulevard, U.S. 1 and nearby interstate exits. Additional ramp closures are also planned later at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway.

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Drivers should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time interstate traffic conditions are available through [Florida 511](https://fl511.com). Updated lane closure information is available through [FDOT District Four](https://www.fdot.gov/info/co/district4).
